title: caltha leptosepala subsp. biflora
intro: Caltha leptosepala subsp. biflora, commonly known as Marsh Marigold, is a perennial herbaceous plant belonging to the family Ranunculaceae. This plant is traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include treating digestive issues and various skin problems due to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Caltha leptosepala subsp. biflora are attributed to its ability to modulate the immune system and exhibit antioxidant activity, thereby providing relief from conditions such as fever and rheumatism. The bioactive constituents responsible for these properties include alkaloids, glycosides, and flavonoids, which have been identified as the primary compounds contributing to the plant's medicinal value.
